label: prf:collatz-no-cycles
title: Proof of collatz no cycles
html:
Proof. Proof of collatz no cycles

Proof (balanced-holonomy sub-case). The Skein-Collatz map is affine, not linear: the odd branch carries an additive term, \mathcal{C}_q(P) = ([3]_q P + 1)/[2]_q, and the even branch is \mathcal{C}_q(P) = P/[2]_q. A periodic orbit of length k with k_{\mathrm{odd}} odd steps and k_{\mathrm{even}} even steps satisfies \mathcal{C}_q^k(P) = P. Iterating the affine steps,

  \mathcal{C}_q^k(P) = A\,P + B,
  \qquad
  A = \frac{[3]_q^{k_{\mathrm{odd}}}}{[2]_q^{k}},
  \qquad
  k = k_{\mathrm{odd}} + k_{\mathrm{even}},

where A = \prod_i a_i is the multiplicative holonomy and B = \sum_i \bigl(\prod_{j>i} a_j\bigr) b_i collects the additive contributions (each b_i = 0 on even steps and b_i = 1/[2]_q^{\,\cdot} > 0 on odd steps, for q > 0). The cycle condition is therefore

  (1 - A)\,P = B.

When A = 1 — i.e. [3]_q^{k_{\mathrm{odd}}} = [2]_q^{k} — the condition forces B = 0. But [2]_q and [3]_q are coprime in \mathbb{Z}[q]: the Skein divisibility identity

  [3]_q - q[2]_q = 1

gives \gcd([2]_q, [3]_q) = 1 by Bézout, so [3]_q is a unit modulo [2]_q while [2]_q^k \equiv 0 \pmod{[2]_q} for k \geq 1 — hence A = 1 is impossible for k_{\mathrm{odd}} \geq 1. The only A = 1 orbit is the all-even chain (k_{\mathrm{odd}} = 0), P \mapsto P/[2]_q^k = P, forcing P = 0. So the coprimality identity excludes every periodic orbit whose holonomy is balanced (A = 1), other than the degenerate fixed point. \square

Scope. This settles only the A = 1 sub-case. The generic cycle has A \neq 1 — indeed coprimality guarantees A \neq 1 for k_{\mathrm{odd}} \geq 1 — and the cycle condition then has a unique candidate solution

  P_0 = \frac{B}{1 - A} \in \mathbb{Q}(q),

positive in the contractive regime (A < 1, i.e. [3]_q^{k_{\mathrm{odd}}} < [2]_q^{k}). Coprimality makes this candidate solvable, not impossible; excluding it requires showing that B/(1-A) never lands in \mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm 1}]_{>0} consistently with its own parity word — the q-analog of classical nontrivial-cycle exclusion, which remains open. A computational census over all primitive parity words through period 18 finds no nontrivial positive cycle: the only Skein-Collatz cycles are the positive 2-cycle \{q^{-1},\, 1 + q^{-1}\} and the negative fixed point -q^{-2}, the q-lifts of the classical \{1, 2\} and \{-1\} respectively.

Classical limit. At q = 1: \gcd(2, 3) = 1 and 3^a \neq 2^b for a, b > 0 (unique prime factorization). The q-deformation lifts this to polynomial coprimality.

The full (a, a+1) family. The identity \gcd([a]_q, [b]_q) = [\gcd(a,b)]_q shows that every Collatz-type map (a, a+1) excludes balanced-holonomy cycles, since \gcd(a, a+1) = 1 for all a. This exclusion is a consequence of consecutive integers being coprime — a fact that lifts from \mathbb{Z} to \mathbb{Z}[q] via the q-integer functor. Like the base case above, it constrains the A = 1 locus and does not by itself reach the affine (A \neq 1) cycle problem.

Open directions. This proposition settles the balanced-holonomy (A = 1) sub-case of cycle exclusion. Two pieces remain open:

  1. Nontrivial-cycle exclusion (A \neq 1): show the candidate P_0 = B/(1-A) never realises a positive Skein-module cycle — the q-analog of classical nontrivial-cycle exclusion.
  2. No divergent orbits: the contact condition \langle v_{[2]} \rangle \geq 2 (contact boundary).
